national.line: H. A. and Margret Rey, the couple behind Curious George, escaped the Nazis during World War II on bicycles, carrying the original manuscripts. Some people really take their work home.
A Missouri dog trainer's dog earned a Guinness World Record for putting clothes pins on a laundry line with her mouth. Finally, some help with the chores.

pride.label: Administrator of the Year
pride.line: Julie Routh, a principal and lifelong Bolivar resident, won the MOSHAPE Administrator of the Year award from Springfield Public Schools. That's a big gold star.

pride.label: $2 Million Milestone
pride.line: The Lake of the Ozarks Idiots Club has passed $2 million in support for local children and youth living in poverty. Those idiots are doing something smart.

pride.label: District Championship
pride.line: Camdenton soccer advanced to the district championship. Time to kick it up a notch.

pride.label: Grand Opening
pride.line: Eye of the Storm Massage celebrated its grand opening with a Bolivar Area Chamber of Commerce ribbon cutting at 290 East Broadway. Business is looking relaxing.

local.line: Japanese students traveled Route 66 through Lebanon. Hope somebody pointed them to the good barbecue.
Lebanon High School students performed 'Much Ado About Nothing.' Much applause about something.
Waynesville R-VI students are celebrating Love of Reading Week through Nov. 6 with a Recycled Robot Contest at East Elementary and a book tasting. Sounds like a delicious week.
Ameren Missouri warns against dumping leaves into Lake of the Ozarks to protect water quality. The lake says leaf it alone.

music.line: Russell Dickerson and his wife Kailey tried a brand-new kind of gender reveal for baby No. 3. Somebody get that baby a guitar.
Stella Lefty is the first country artist since Taylor Swift to perform at Capital's Jingle Bell Ball. That's some Swift company.
Randy Travis will be honored at the Grand Ole Opry for his 40-year milestone. Forty years and still going.
Dolly Parton's new holiday collectible, a plush doll called 'Dolly on the Holly,' is now available at Walmart. Stocking stuffer, meet your queen.
Terri Clark says she has no plans to retire from country music anytime soon. Good, we're not done listening.
A lost 1970 sci-fi film called 'Saturation 70' was meant to star Gram Parsons and country clothier Nudie Cohn. Rhinestones in space, anyone?
Jessica Chastain premiered her new country music movie 'Heartland' in New York City and explained why she won't be singing on Broadway. The audience can relax.
Morgan Wallen announced his 'Sand In My Boots' festival returns to Gulf Shores, Alabama, after taking 2026 off. Pack sunscreen and a bigger wallet.

weird.line: An emu on the loose in Connecticut was captured and reunited with its owner. Somebody needs a taller fence.
A Menasha, Wisconsin, fisherman shattered a 76-year-old state record with a smallmouth bass. Now that's a fish story with paperwork.
An alligator went viral after casually strolling into a North Carolina bagel shop like a customer. Someone wanted a bagel with a bite.
Claude Moore's rubber band ball weighs 11,578 pounds and beats a 2008 record. That's one stretch of a hobby.
Austin firefighters rescued a raccoon that got its head stuck in a tree. Curiosity, meet branch.
Firefighters rescued a deer that fell into a partially drained backyard pool at a Michigan home. Somebody wanted a late swim.
A coyote was caught on camera crossing the 101 Wildlife Bridge. Finally, someone using the crosswalk.
A rare all-white porcupine was caught on video crossing a road in Vermont. Not your average roadside visitor.
A mammoth fossil found in Acadiana, Louisiana, reveals the state's Ice Age past. That's one old bone.
A rare Montana-found dinosaur fossil sold for $47.3 million at auction. That's one expensive bone.
A North Carolina man says a malfunctioning printer at a gas pump led to his winning $2 million from a Powerball drawing. Sometimes the pump pays you back.
A Transformers-themed band called the Cybertronic Spree performed a psychedelic cover of Black Sabbath's 'War Pigs.' Autobots, roll out the amps.
A backyard video in Austin, Texas, shows raccoons playfully tugging on a thirsty skunk's tail. Brave, or just rude.
A black bear paid a surprise visit outside a home near Santa Barbara, California. Hope he wiped his paws.
A young black bear was spotted getting into trash in Lawrence Township. Dinner delivery, bear style.
Scientists say they discovered dinosaur blood in a 115-million-year-old fossil. Talk about a blood-curdling find.
Scientists cracked the code on a treasure ship's padlock, solving a 400-year-old maritime mystery. Finally, someone found the key.
Murray Family Farms' pumpkin patch saw record attendance ahead of its final Saturday. That's a gourd turnout.
A bear was spotted in Abington. Hope the neighbors locked the trash.

humor.line: Inventor James Naismith nailed peach baskets ten feet up in a YMCA gym, and the first game used a soccer ball with nine players per team. Nothing but peach.
A Fort Lauderdale business attorney created it in 2001, and it bans lawyer jokes and lawyer bashing. No objections here.
Ballpark nachos with jalapenos and melted cheese were invented by Sal and Margarita Manriquez, who sold them at the Dallas State Fair in 1964. Cheesy beginnings, nobody's complaining.
Adolphe Sax's saxophones were originally designed for military bands, but they ended up in orchestras too. Not bad for a band instrument.
People celebrate by getting purposely lost and finding their way back without a compass. Some of us practice this daily.
The teddy bear was named for President Theodore Roosevelt after a cartoon showed him refusing to shoot a bear on a 1902 hunting trip. Best photo-op a bear ever had.
In 1973 New Jersey became the first state to let girls play Little League, after 11-year-old Marcia Pepe of Hoboken played three games for her team. Play ball.
Dark chocolate needs at least 35% cocoa solids, which makes this the healthier cousin of the July milk chocolate day. We'll call it health food.
The word 'notary' comes from 'nota,' a shorthand invented by Cicero's clerk to take down Cicero's speeches. Someone had to write down all that talking.
Books began as clay tablets and papyrus, with writing on clay dating back to the third millennium BCE. Today's paperbacks are way lighter.
Puns show up in Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian and Mayan hieroglyphics, so groaners go back thousands of years. Turns out dad jokes are ancient history.
Cappuccino is named for the reddish-brown hooded robes of Capuchin friars, since cappuccio means 'hood' in Italian. Your coffee is wearing a hoodie.
Cooking tools linked to pupusas were found at Joya de Cerén, a site buried by volcanic ash about 2,000 years ago. That's a very old family recipe.
Dr. Seuss's 'Fox in Socks' and 'Oh Say Can You Say?' are packed with tongue twisters. Good luck reading them fast to your kids.
In Minsk, pianist Nikolai Panok once played for six hours without stopping. His fingers deserve a day off.
Creators Thomas and Ruth Roy of Wellcat say don't forget the sauerkraut and garlic. Pack extra breath mints.
Early British puddings were savory, some made with meat and cooked in an animal stomach. Sticky toffee sounds better.
Carl Sagan's 1980 PBS series 'Cosmos' was the most widely viewed PBS program of its time. He made space look good on TV.
The fried chicken sandwich took off because it lets you eat fried chicken with clean hands. Napkins still recommended.
Scrapple was created by the Pennsylvania Dutch, who came to America from Germany and Switzerland in the 17th and 18th centuries. Don't ask questions, just eat.
Greek yogurt is regular yogurt that's been strained to remove whey, which makes it thicker and creamier. Yogurt that went through the strainer.
Area codes were devised by AT&T in the 1940s and fully rolled out in 1947. Today, call someone with a different one.
The word 'cupcake' was first used in 1828, and an early cupcake-like dessert appeared in a cookbook in 1796. Sweet history in a tiny package.
In 2009 New York City briefly renamed a corner '123 Sesame Street,' and a permanent sign went up in 2019. Counting on that sign to stay.
Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli, born in 1445, wrote a printed math book that was the first to include double-entry bookkeeping. He's why the books balance.
Pocky Day lands on 11/11 because the long, thin snacks look like the number one. That's a lot of ones to snack on.
Singles' Day began in 1993 when four male students at Nanjing University in China decided to make being single more exciting. Fitting date: four ones.
National Metal Day is on 11/11 because of the Spinal Tap amps that go up to 11, and VH1 Classic first proclaimed it in 2011. This one goes to 11.
One story says sundaes started in Two Rivers, Wisconsin, in 1881, and a Manitowoc fountain owner served them only on Sundays. Sundays have always been sweet.
